title: Pair CSR and packed-bitset timing policy and retain the crossover diagnostic
finding: The packed-bitset arm used warmup plus repeated median timing, while the stdlib CSR oracle was timed exactly once. Ratios therefore mixed a sampled hot-path denominator with a single potentially cold/noisy reference observation. In addition, the calibration was printed to transient job logs only, so the exact numeric diagnostic was harder to retain and re-check than the surrounding contract evidence.
change: add one local repeated-measurement helper and reuse the existing MAX_REPEATS/MAX_WARMUP bounds
apply the same warmup and repeat counts to the stdlib TypedRelationBlock.matmul Boolean reference and the resident packed-bitset kernel in the same process
bump the diagnostic wire schema from daedalus-tensor-cpu-bitset-baseline/1 to /2 rather than silently changing its timing meaning
report median/min/max/sample count for the CSR reference and packed-bitset kernel
rename diagnostic ratios so they explicitly compare a full CSR operation to either the resident bitset kernel or the bitset one-shot path
retain the exact bounded Python 3.12/hash-0 JSON diagnostic as a seven-day GitHub Actions artifact inside the existing Fourfold/Tensor workflow

gardener.reason_for_artifact_step: retain the already-running bounded calibration as replayable evidence instead of adding another benchmark harness

verification.python_312_hash_0: integrated contracts, equal-sample CPU calibration, diagnostic artifact upload and public API smoke succeeded
verification.repository_collection: success; collection-only, not a full-suite execution claim

interpretation: All six frozen cases reproduced exact Boolean support and matching canonical digests against the stdlib CSR oracle.
The resident packed-bitset kernel was much cheaper than the full reference operation in this synthetic runner matrix, but that is diagnostic evidence rather than a general backend superiority claim.

The one-shot crossover is workload dependent: the smallest sparse 64-node case loses after packing/canonicalization, the 128-node sparse case is effectively break-even, and the denser/larger retained cases have ratios above one on this runner.

At 256 nodes and roughly 5 percent density, canonical reconstruction consumed 21.179875 ms of the 22.798462 ms one-shot path. The next optimization question is therefore output representation/reuse, not another arithmetic kernel layer.
CUDA still has to beat the packed-bitset baseline under the same exact case and must account for transfer, allocation and readback; no GPU result exists yet.
next: Before adding another execution backend, test whether retaining packed rows and/or returning a lightweight support view can remove the measured one-shot canonicalization cost without creating a second authoritative relation representation. Then run the existing CUDA arm on owner NVIDIA hardware against the same frozen cases.
